title: Keys
summary: Major and minor scales, key signatures, and how keys are related.

lessons.title: How a major scale is built
lessons.summary: One pattern of whole and half steps gives every major scale.

blocks.text: Every major scale follows the same pattern of steps: whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half. Start on C and the pattern lands on white keys only. Start on any other note and you need black keys to keep the pattern.
Each letter name is used exactly once. That is why G major has F♯ rather than G♭: the scale already has a G, and it needs some kind of F.
G major: the seventh note is F♯.

exercise.prompt: Where are the half steps in a major scale?
exercise.explanation: Whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half: the half steps fall between 3–4 and 7–8.

blocks.text: Work out the note from the pattern.

lessons.title: Key signatures
lessons.summary: Sharps and flats arrive in a fixed order.

blocks.text: A key signature at the start of each line tells you which notes are sharp or flat throughout the piece, so they do not have to be marked every time.
Sharps are always added in the same order: F, C, G, D, A, E, B. Each new sharp key starts a fifth higher than the last: C (none), G (one), D (two), A (three), E (four).

Flats are added in the opposite order: B, E, A, D, G, C, F. Each new flat key starts a fifth lower: C (none), F (one), B♭ (two), E♭ (three), A♭ (four). Arranged in a ring, this is the circle of fifths.

exercise.explanation: The order of sharps starts with F♯. G major has just that one.

exercise.prompt: D major has two sharps. Which are they?
exercise.explanation: The first two sharps in order: F♯ and C♯.

lessons.title: Minor keys
lessons.summary: Every major key has a minor partner with the same signature.

blocks.text: Each major key shares its key signature with one minor key, called its relative minor. The relative minor starts on the sixth note of the major scale, which is three half steps below the major keynote. C major and A minor share a signature; so do G major and E minor.
A natural minor: the notes of C major, starting on A.

Minor-key music usually raises the seventh note by a half step so that it leads firmly back to the keynote. The key signature does not show this, so it appears as a sharp or natural written in the music. In A minor it is G♯.

exercise.prompt: What is the relative minor of C major?
exercise.explanation: The sixth note of C major is A.

exercise.prompt: What is the relative minor of G major?
exercise.explanation: The sixth note of G major is E. Both keys have one sharp.

blocks.text: Minor keys use their relative major's signature.
Für Elise is in A minor too: look for the raised seventh, G♯.
